reason: I’ll start fitting the digestive tube with the salivary glands, which contribute to breaking down starch.
expectation: The glands will be added to the digestive tube, leaving the other slots to fill.

alternatives.reason: Starting starch digestion also seems useful, but I want to assemble the organs first.

effect: The glands are fitted, and the description confirms that saliva begins starch digestion. I’ll continue assembling the organs.
reaction: The result was expected and made the glands’ role clear.
reason: The pancreas supplies digestive juices, so fitting it advances the organ assembly goal.
expectation: The pancreas will be added to the digestive tube, leaving the liver and gallbladder to fit.

alternatives.reason: The liver and gallbladder also belong in the tube, but I’ll add the pancreas first.

effect: The pancreas is fitted, so I can continue assembling the digestive organs.
reaction: The fitting was expected; there was no new explanation.
reason: Adding the liver and gallbladder advances the organ assembly goal.
expectation: The liver and gallbladder will be fitted to the digestive tube; the portal vessel slot may still remain.

alternatives.reason: I could begin starch digestion, but I want to finish fitting the available organs first.

effect: The liver and gallbladder are fitted, completing the organ assembly goal. I can now focus on breaking down the meal.
reaction: The fitting was expected, though it added no new explanation.
reason: Salivary amylase begins starch digestion, so this starts the remaining goal.
expectation: The starch will be partly broken down, possibly needing further digestion before absorption.

alternatives.reason: Protein digestion also advances the goal, but I’ll start with the starch route introduced by the salivary glands.

effect: Salivary amylase produced shorter starch chains, so the starch needs further digestion.
reaction: The result was expected, though it offered little explanation beyond the picture.
reason: I’ll continue the starch route with the remaining digestive enzymes.
expectation: The shorter chains will be broken into smaller sugars suitable for absorption.

alternatives.reason: Protein digestion also advances the meal goal, but I want to finish the starch route first.

effect: The starch route produced individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining; I’ll move on to the other foods.
reaction: That clearly connected starch breakdown to absorption.
reason: Protein-digesting enzymes should break down the protein portion of the meal.
expectation: The protein will be broken into smaller components suitable for absorption, perhaps after further digestion.

alternatives.reason: Fat also needs digestion, but I’ll tackle protein first.

effect: Protein digestion produced amino acids, leaving fat as the only offered food combination.
reaction: The result was expected, though it gave no further explanation.
reason: I’ll use the only available combination to break down the fat portion of the meal.
expectation: Bile and lipase will help break fat into smaller components for absorption.

effect: Fat digestion produced fatty acids and monoglycerides, completing the meal breakdown goal. The explanation clarified the different roles of bile and lipase.
reaction: The distinction between dispersing fat and breaking its molecules apart was useful and specific.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking down fat was the most worthwhile action: the result clearly distinguished bile's role from lipase's and corrected a possible misconception that bile is an enzyme.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the pancreas and then the liver and gallbladder felt repetitive. The results confirmed progress but added no explanation at either step.

surprise.text: The fat result made me think more carefully about bile: it disperses fat into droplets rather than acting as an enzyme.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely arbitrary, though the separate organ fittings were predictable and offered little sense of a meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing to see how the digested nutrients cross the gut and reach the body, though the repeated fittings made this chapter feel mechanical.
